heading: EXT. DRAINED MUNICIPAL SWIMMING POOL - DAY

units.text: EXT. DRAINED MUNICIPAL SWIMMING POOL - DAY
A company retreat held in the deep end of a decommissioned pool.
Folding chairs are arranged in a circle on the sloped floor, tilted slightly toward the drain.
Lane lines coil in a corner like dead snakes.
A banner on the diving board reads: SYNERGY THROUGH SPLASH.
FACILITATOR PRIYA DESHMUKH-WALL, 40s, tailored linen, a headset mic taped to her cheek, stands in the exact center on the drain cover.

Around her sit four employees: BARNES, 50s, sales director, in a polo with a company crest; LEOCADIA, 30s, product lead, cross-legged on her chair; WITOLD, 20s, an intern sipping an iced coffee; and DESMOND "DEZ" ROUSE, 40s, finance, who tugs at his collar and checks his watch every ninety seconds.
Everyone, I want you to close your eyes and picture water. Warm, clear, still water.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: It's a pool.
units.name: BARNES

units.text: It's a drained pool.
units.name: LEOCADIA

units.text: Can I picture the empty version?
units.name: WITOLD

units.text: You may picture whatever serves you.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Priya paces a slow arc around the circle, her sandals slapping on the tile.
Barnes opens one eye and peeks at Dez.
Dez peeks back.
Leocadia sips her water bottle and rearranges her crossed legs.
Witold's chair tilts and he catches the diving-board ladder with one hand without opening his eyes.
We've done this twice already.
units.name: DEZ

units.text: Dez, I'm hearing resistance.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: I'm hearing a leaf blower.
units.name: DEZ

units.text: Everyone listens.
A distant whine over the pool wall.
Priya smiles, patient.
We call that the sound of the world continuing.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Can we get to the part with the numbers?
units.name: BARNES

units.text: There are no numbers today.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Then why am I here?
units.name: BARNES

units.text: Because you want to be seen.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Barnes folds his arms.
A long silence.
Witold's iced coffee crackles as the ice shifts.
Leocadia clears her throat and raises her hand like a schoolchild.
Priya, I think I'm going to say something and I need everyone to just let me.
units.name: LEOCADIA

units.text: This is a safe deep end.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: We lost the Hartwell contract. Last Tuesday. The CEO told us not to say anything.
units.name: LEOCADIA

units.text: The circle stiffens.
Barnes' arms drop.
Dez stops fiddling with his collar.
Witold lowers his coffee.
Oh God.
units.name: DEZ

units.text: How do you know?
units.name: BARNES

units.text: I wrote the termination letter.
units.name: LEOCADIA

units.text: A beat.
Priya, for the first time all morning, says nothing at all.
The leaf blower whines on, rising and falling.
Then Barnes begins, slowly, to laugh.
He wheezes, shoulders shaking, tears in his eyes, and the others catch it one by one, even Dez, even Witold, a ragged communal howl that echoes off the tile.
I think we've just had a breakthrough.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Priya, we've had a firing.
units.name: BARNES
